scope: Source-derived development verification lanes and exact-once STRICT test union; documentation identity-only Browser QA; concise non-authoritative recovery checkpoints. Preview-only, paid execution disabled.
riskAnalysis: Verification control changes are critical: false-low classification or stale evidence could omit mandatory security tests. Default unknown/shared/executable/dependency changes to STRICT; preserve owner preflight and independent acceptance.

threatModel.assets: Mandatory security/contract tests, source/release identity, immutable evidence, owner authority and historical budget accounting.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Actual Git history to lane selection; source-derived plan to CI jobs; protected Preview identity to browser scope; recorded checkpoint to resumed agent.
threatModel.abuseCases: Disguised dependency, renamed/deleted protected source, active CSS/HTML, stale plan, mutated source during test, skipped security scan labelled passed, or old authority observation treated as permission.
threatModel.mitigations: Complete no-renames diff, canonical paths/modes, both-tree protected-consumer checks, conservative active-content rejection, exact head/tree before and after execution, explicit scope labels, immutable release pin, no evidence-cache permissions.

rollback: Keep paid false. Revert only verification optimization on feature branch if gates fail; preserve full default npm test/live preflight and all historical evidence. Never change Production or authorization.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Independent policy regressions cover malformed-response where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.stale-state: Independent policy regressions cover stale-state where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.concurrency: Independent policy regressions cover concurrency where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.cancellation: Independent policy regressions cover cancellation where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Independent policy regressions cover worker-interruption where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.api-outage: Independent policy regressions cover api-outage where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Independent policy regressions cover authorization-denial where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.
negativePaths.spending-limit: No spending code or approval changes. Every lane has paidPermission false; existing budget and live preflight remain authoritative.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Independent policy regressions cover partial-execution where applicable through actual Git fixtures, stale/altered plan rejection and retained mandatory STRICT tests; no owner/runtime control is removed.

defects.rootCause: CI executed standalone contract groups and24 named groups before a full suite containing the same tests; documentation Browser QA repeated502 captures.
defects.detectionGap: Prior readiness focused on coverage and missed execution duplication and distinction between documentation checkpoints and application visual changes.
defects.regression: Independent lane/hidden dependency/active content/stale plan/mode/rename tests and exact-once mandatory contract membership; actual final documentation workflow will measure identity-only behavior.
defects.historicalPrevention: The source union and Git-derived docs classification detect prior redundant composition without treating skipped checks as fresh verification.

proactiveReview.architecture: Existing quality gate and contract list remain authoritative; one selector/runner and lightweight affected public checker, no parallel agent executor.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Node builtins and already pinned Playwright; no new packages, credentials, paid transport or customer mutations.
proactiveReview.threats: Low-risk concealment, escaped CSS, entity/active HTML, missing history, stale source, mismatched deployment, unsafe header forwarding and misleading cached evidence.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Selection errors stop rather than downgrade; source changes during tests reject evidence; manual Browser reruns force STRICT; failure artifacts preserved.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Actual temporary Git histories, both-tree consumers, rename/delete/modes, altered plans, executable/dependency content, false authority and workflow gating.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Separate QA authored adversarial tests; Auditor identified CSS/HTML escapes, manual dispatch base, end-of-run source drift and metadata false positives; corrections independently reviewed.
proactiveReview.recovery: Concise source-bound recovery pointer with exact next action and observation age; no new authorization window; revert feature verification changes safely.
proactiveReview.readiness: Full optimization change itself is STRICT; run frozen full union, independent reviews, Redis/CI/CodeQL and exact hosted full Browser QA, then measure docs identity-only lane. Affected lane remains separately qualified.
